an3.80:4.2: _Goyāna_ (“cow-cart”) is probably corrupt, as no Goyāna is found elsewhere. The Sanskrit spelling is _godānīya_, “cow-donation”, i.e. a land abundant in the wealth typified by cows. Now, _godānīya_ is a mere verbal variation of _godāvarī_, the name of the famed river that arises near modern Mumbai on the west coast ([snp5.1:2.3]()). Lands further west were reached by ship from that shore. I think this is an ancient corruption and should read “west of Godāvarī”.
an3.80:9.1: The lack of vocative in what follows indicates that this was not addressed to anyone, per Thai editions.
